programme.title: iShowSpeed Carribean Tour 2026
programme.desc: IShowSpeed travels to Guadeloupe for the first time, exploring the island’s culture, communities, and vibrant energy. Along the way, Speed embraces a playful challenge as he’s humorously welcomed as the island’s “president,” leading to unforgettable interactions and larger-than-life moments. Blending cultural discovery, comedy, and his signature chaos, the episode captures an entertaining journey through one of the Caribbean’s most unique destinations.

programme.title: iShowSpeed China Tour
programme.desc: IShowSpeed travels to Chongqing, one of China’s most unique and visually stunning cities. Known for its towering skyline, mountainous landscape, and vibrant street life, Chongqing offers Speed a completely new experience around every corner. From exploring the city’s famous landmarks and local culture to navigating its bustling streets and unforgettable atmosphere, the episode captures an unfiltered adventure through one of China’s most dynamic urban destinations.

programme.title: iShowSpeed Carribean Tour 2026
programme.desc: IShowSpeed travels to Dominica and immerses himself in the traditions of the Kalinago people, the Caribbean’s last remaining Indigenous community. From learning about their history and customs to experiencing daily life and cultural practices firsthand, Speed gains a unique perspective on one of the region’s richest cultural legacies. Blending discovery, connection, and his signature energy, the episode captures an unforgettable journey through Dominica and the traditions that continue to shape its identity.

programme.title: iShowSpeed Carribean Tour 2026
programme.desc: IShowSpeed travels to Jamaica alongside global music stars Shenseea and Sean Paul, experiencing the culture, energy, and influence of one of the Caribbean’s most iconic nations. From exploring local hotspots and connecting with residents to immersing himself in the music, food, and traditions that define the island, Speed gets a firsthand look at Jamaica through the eyes of two of its biggest ambassadors. Blending adventure, entertainment, and his signature chaos, the episode captures an unforgettable journey through the heart of Jamaican culture.

programme.title: iShowSpeed China Tour
programme.desc: IShowSpeed experiences the ancient art of Mongolian throat singing, immersing himself in one of the country's most unique and celebrated cultural traditions. Guided by talented local performers, Speed learns how singers produce multiple tones at once while discovering the history and significance of this centuries-old musical practice. From hilarious attempts to master the technique to unforgettable performances, the episode blends cultural discovery, entertainment, and Speed's signature energy, offering a rare look into one of Mongolia's most extraordinary artistic traditions.

programme.title: iShowSpeed Carribean Tour 2026
programme.desc: IShowSpeed takes on one of his most intense experiences yet as he goes shark diving in the crystal-clear waters of the Bahamas. Coming face-to-face with some of the ocean’s most powerful predators, Speed pushes past his fears and experiences the thrill of the underwater world firsthand. Blending adrenaline, adventure, and his signature chaos, the episode captures an unforgettable journey through one of the Caribbean’s most breathtaking marine environments.

programme.title: iShowSpeed Africa Tour 2025/6
programme.desc: IShowSpeed travels to Ghana for the first time, experiencing a vibrant culture filled with music, energy, and community. From exploring the streets and connecting with locals to taking in everyday life and traditions, Speed immerses himself in everything Ghana has to offer. Blending curiosity, chaos, and real-time reactions, the episode captures an unfiltered journey through one of West Africa’s most dynamic and welcoming countries.

programme.title: iShowSpeed Carribean Tour 2026
programme.desc: IShowSpeed travels to Barbados for the first time, experiencing the island’s vibrant culture, beautiful scenery, and unique energy. From exploring local hotspots and meeting residents to taking in the food, music, and atmosphere, Speed immerses himself in everything Barbados has to offer. Blending curiosity, adventure, and his signature chaos, the episode captures an unfiltered journey through one of the Caribbean’s most iconic destinations.

programme.desc: From personal dramas to scientific uproars, it's been a wild year for the biggest health & fitness podcaster in the world. And today we get to discover his biggest new insights about life, relationships and protocols. Expect to learn whether you actually should drink coffee within 90 minutes of waking up, how to get the best sleep of your life according to the latest science, how to become a morning person, what Andrew has learned about the perils of fame and public scrutiny, what new research says on the world of longevity supplements, why you should always do your research when testing with peptides and much more…

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.desc: Expect to learn what “Don’t half-ass it” means, the story of how Matthew got his iconic starting role in Dazed & Confused, how to see the upside during any crisis, why having a sense of humour should be your default emotion, McConaughey’s own version of his Lonely Chapter, when you should listen to your gut versus your head, why McConaughey turned down $14.5M to pursue something great, Matthew's reflections on the 10 year anniversary of Interstellar, lesson on finding the perfect partner, and much more…

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.desc: Hustle culture often tells us that working harder is the only way to succeed—grinding through 80-hour weeks on 4 hours of sleep per night. But what if the real solution isn’t about working harder, but finding balance? What if true success lies in slowing down, savouring life, smoking a cigar on the porch occasionally and being fully present. How differently might we define success then? Expect to learn who Dry Creek Dewayne’s is, his backstory and upbringing, how to un-harden yourself, how any person can overcome & control their anger, what Dewayne has learned from working with horses, the dangers of being out of balance in work & life, how to have a better relationship with the voice in your head, how to find the right partner & why men need to learn to treat women better, why bad fathers are partly to blame for the downfall of America’s culture, what a day in the life of Dewayne’s life is like and much more…

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.desc: These days, making sense of the world is harder than ever. From billionaires reshaping governments to debates over whether modern car chassis can support the average obese person. There’s no shortage of absurdities. Luckily, Tom has plenty to say about them. Expect to learn why Gen Z is more likely to skip the gym and use Ozempic instead, if Tom can and will reset his Instagram algorithm, why Gen Z is more likely to drink less and smoke more, why the younger generation is sexless than most, Tom’s thoughts on Elon’s current rampage through government bureaucracy, Tom’s recent obsession with True Crime documentaries, why being competent is a curse and much more…

programme.title: Pod Save America
programme.desc: Pete Hegseth, in an unconventional speech, announces that beardos, weirdos, and wimps are no longer welcome at the Department of War as his boss officially hit the road to campaign for Senate Republicans — whether they want him to or not. Jon and Dan react to Trump's event with Ken Paxton in Texas, Trump proclaiming his love for data centers in a wide-ranging interview with TIME, and Missouri Senator Eric Schmitt's embarrassing mix-up in a Judiciary Committee hearing with former Special Counsel Jack Smith. Then, Rev. Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Kansas, talks to Dan about what it'll take to elect the state's first Democratic senator in nearly 100 years, and why he considers himself both a liberal and a conservative.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.desc: The midterms are next month, and President Donald Trump's approval rating on issues like the economy is slipping. But are Democrats capitalizing on it? Is their messaging keeping pace with the moment? On today's show, Jane sits down with Sarah Longwell to discuss how Democrats can communicate their policy ideas more effectively and connect with voters. Longwell is the author of the new book, How to Eat an Elephant: One Voter at a Time.

programme.title: Runaway Country with Alex Wagner
programme.desc: As the electoral landscape is turning blue, Donald Trump is seeing red. To sooth his wounded ego, the White House is running pro-Trump ads during NFL games, illegally rescinding hundreds of millions of dollars from federal agencies, and threatening the Kennedy Performing Arts Center with demolition for not adding Trump’s name to the facade. To understand the cost of the president's flailing narcissism, Alex chats with Leonard Slatkin, the former conductor of the National Symphony Orchestra—now on involuntary tour since the Kennedy Center's closure. Then, she is joined by historian and On Tyranny author, Timothy Snyder, to discuss what else we can expect from this late stage autocrat.

programme.title: Hysteria
programme.desc: Erin and KQED’s Marisa Lagos take a look at the democrats’' national polling surge, analyze the heck is going on in California politics, and look into the horrific yet familiar Cornell 7 sexual assault case. Then labor economist Kathryn Anne Edwards joins to demystify everything from the job market to the AI bubble. They wrap up with a petty conversation about the WNBA finals and killer e-bikes.

programme.title: Strict Scrutiny
programme.desc: In the fifth and final installment of our Hot Supreme Court Reform series, Kate speaks with Gabe Roth, executive director of Fix the Court. What would a meaningful and enforceable set of ethics rules look like for the Supreme Court justices? Why isn’t there an Inspector General for the judiciary? How are there no real rules around recusals? Roth makes the case for these nonpartisan reforms and more.

programme.title: Offline with Jon Favreau
programme.desc: From underground compounds to planet-fleeing rockets, tech oligarchs and the MAGA elite aren’t just anticipating an apocalypse—they’re hastening it. Author and climate activist Naomi Klein sits down with Jon to discuss End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World, her new book with Astra Taylor. She and Jon trace the connection between the religious right, Silicon Valley elite, and nationalist movements around the world, and uncover how Donald Trump and J.D. Vance are weaponizing the very human instinct to protect our own. Then they discuss how to make people feel safer, less prone to zero-sum thinking, and more invested in a future we have to share.

programme.title: Offline with Jon Favreau (If AI Might Kill Us All, Why Are We Still Building It?)
programme.desc: Max Fisher returns to Offline to face the robot apocalypse with Jon. The two discuss Jacob Coxon, the AI researcher who publicly resigned from Anthropic this week, the terrifying claims coming from those working in AI that the technology may kill us all, and what it'll take for politicians to actually attempt to regulate the fast-moving technology. But first: Jon shares an exciting announcement about the future of the show.
